events.title: The attack on Pope Leo III
events.shortBlurb: Assailants of the late pope's kindred fell upon Leo III in the procession of the Greater Litanies…
body: On 25 April 799, as Pope Leo III rode in the procession of the Greater Litanies toward the Flaminian Gate, armed men of the late Pope Hadrian I's kindred set upon him, dashed him to the ground, and strove to tear out his eyes and his tongue, leaving him bleeding in the street.

Leo, a Roman of humble birth, cardinal-priest of Santa Susanna, had been elected on 26 December 795, the very day of Hadrian's burial, and had sought Charlemagne's friendship from the first, sending him the keys of St. Peter's confession and the standard of the city. His enemies accused him to the Frankish king; held in the monastery of St. Erasmus on the Caelian, he recovered the use of his eyes and tongue — in what the old biographies relate as miraculous — escaped, and made his way to Charlemagne at Paderborn, who received him with the highest honor.

Restored to Rome in November 799 under Frankish guard, he purged himself by oath of his accusers' charges on 23 December 800; two days later, at Mass on Christmas Day, he crowned Charlemagne emperor of the Romans — an act that remade the map of Europe and bound the papacy to the West.
